title: Suitability and quality of the measures to maximise expected outcomes and impacts, as set out in the dissemination and exploitation plan, including communication activities
content:
## 2.2 Suitability and quality of the measures to maximise expected outcomes and impacts, as set out in the dissemination and exploitation plan, including communication activities

### Proportionality and design principle

FIELDWISE is a single-beneficiary MSCA European Fellowship hosted by HUN-REN ATK, so its dissemination, exploitation and communication measures are deliberately scaled to what one experienced researcher, working with an associated-partner environment (ELTE, MATE, Krumatic) and a non-academic placement host (AgroVIR), can credibly deliver in 30 months. The plan avoids the over-scaled ambitions typical of large consortia and instead attaches each activity to a concrete project output already defined in the work plan, so that every measure is verifiable through a named deliverable and a Key Performance Indicator. Three audiences are addressed in a graded way: the scientific community (dissemination), agricultural practitioners and the general public (communication), and the technology-uptake chain of software providers and farm-management information system (FMIS) integrators (exploitation). This mirrors the call's own logic, which asks the fellowship to increase and broaden research and innovation impact through enhanced networking and communication with scientific peers and the general public (EO-03/EI-03), and to strengthen knowledge transfer and R&I capacity among participating organisations (EI-06).

### Dissemination plan and target groups (scientific community)

Scientific dissemination is anchored in peer-reviewed publication and in the reusable, well-documented artefacts the research itself produces. The action targets at least two high-quality peer-reviewed publications, with a possible third methods/application paper if the independent commercial-field dataset supports it. The scientific value is concentrated in two artefacts that are engineered to be citable and reusable rather than internal: the model card released within D2.1 Primary model, benchmark and model card (due M14), which reports the primary model and nonlinear benchmark with calibration, uncertainty, interpretability and blocked unseen-year performance; and the crop-transfer specification released within D2.2 Spectral/UAV/Sentinel harmonisation, scaling and crop-transfer specification (due M14), which enumerates the transferable core components, crop-specific parameters, minimum validation data and recalibration gates required to add a new crop. The prospective transferability finding — including any transfer loss, stated rather than hidden — is a scientific result in its own right and is disseminated through the WP3 report. Dissemination follows an open-science posture of 'as open as possible, as closed as necessary', with methods, metadata and publications made reusable and FAIR where the commercial-sensitivity constraints on farmer and MATE-derived data allow. Dissemination into higher education is delivered through a teaching route of short guest lectures, seminars and practical sessions at MATE and, where institutionally possible, the Agricultural University of Plovdiv, transferring the fellow's prior university teaching into the new discipline of agricultural data science; this addresses EI-06 despite ATK being a research organisation rather than a university. Target groups here are plant-physiology, crop-modelling, remote-sensing/Earth-observation and precision-agriculture research communities, and students at the named teaching venues.

### Communication activities and target groups (practitioners and the public)

Communication is practitioner- and public-facing and is scaled to a single fellow. It comprises practitioner-oriented demonstrations of the stress and uncertainty outputs, at least one public-facing article per year, and — through Krumatic — farmer-facing demonstrations and communication in Bulgaria, using the software partner's established Bulgarian deployment channel to reach growers directly. A possible public-facing demonstration at the planned Szentendre Skanzen model garden, linking traditional horticultural knowledge with modern sensing, is held as a contingent, complementary opportunity that will be pursued only if the garden is formally established and scientifically suitable. These activities respond to EI-03 (broadened public engagement) and situate the work within its wider societal frame — the fellowship contributes particularly to SDG 2, SDG 6, SDG 12 and SDG 13, and communication messaging is disciplined to avoid an unearned numeric water-saving promise, reporting instead the quantities the project actually measures. Target groups are commercial vegetable growers (in Hungary and Bulgaria), agronomic advisors, and the interested public.

### Exploitation plan and target groups (uptake chain)

Exploitation is organised around the DrR web MVP as the tangible route from validated research to external testing. WP4 (DrR Web MVP, Co-development and Exploitation Preparation) delivers D4.1 Crop-configurable DrR web MVP with validated processing-tomato module (due M24) and D4.2 Pre-placement technical/usability requirements dossier (due M24); the architecture is deliberately crop-configurable so that the reusable data-ingestion, uncertainty, visualisation and irrigation-attention components can carry later crop modules once crop-specific validation exists, rather than universalising from tomato. The exploitation pathway is then hardened by the non-academic placement: WP5 (AgroVIR Non-Academic Placement) delivers D5.1 AgroVIR operational/interoperability assessment (due M30) and D5.2 Post-MSCA FMIS integration and exploitation roadmap (due M30), the latter naming the required interfaces, the exploitation route and the concrete post-fellowship steps toward FMIS integration. AgroVIR's involvement supplies requirements-oriented consultation from project start and an operational evaluator whose relevance is commercial rather than scientific, and the placement is supervised by Miklós Maróti; the fellow works with the AgroVIR product development team responsible for the FMIS platform. Beyond the funded period, a defined post-MSCA replication and transferability route through MVCRI provides a Bulgarian recalibration-and-extension pathway, and Krumatic supports Bulgarian farmer-facing uptake. Target groups for exploitation are FMIS providers and agricultural-software developers (AgroVIR, Krumatic), and, through them, commercial growers of irrigated high-value horticulture.

### Intellectual-property management and foreseen protection measures

The IP strategy rests on a clean separation of rights layers that is made explicit throughout the concept: the fellow's pre-existing DrR - Digital Agronomist background is kept distinct from FIELDWISE foreground, from institutional datasets, and from Krumatic-developed code, with each layer requiring its own documentation before the action starts. As a concrete protection and hygiene measure, task T4.6 maintains a background/foreground and data/IP inventory across the action, and risk R10 commits the project to using MATE-derived assets only for approved research and to conducting an institutional data-rights/IP assessment before any commercial exploitation. The fellow's independent, self-financed authorship of DrR — with no MVCRI ownership position — is the stated background position, to be hardened by a dated DrR background declaration and version inventory (with deposit, e.g. on Zenodo, as an option) before the action begins. Ownership of placement results follows the grant-agreement default, vesting in HUN-REN ATK as beneficiary acting through the fellow, to be confirmed by a written placement agreement between the fellow, HUN-REN ATK and AgroVIR concluded before the placement, which will also fix the access terms to the fellow's DrR background IP; Krumatic's code-IP terms are settled in a development agreement before the action starts. These measures are proportionate: they are documentation and agreement instruments rather than patent-scale protection, which matches a software-and-methodology fellowship whose value lies in validated, reusable know-how.

### Fit to expected outcomes and impacts

Taken together, these measures give each of the call's impact and outcome expectations a concrete, deliverable-backed mechanism: dissemination through the model card, crop-transfer specification, publications and teaching route serves EI-06; communication through practitioner demonstrations, annual public articles and Bulgarian farmer-facing outreach serves EI-03/EO-03; and exploitation through the DrR web MVP, the AgroVIR operational assessment, the post-MSCA FMIS roadmap and the MVCRI replication route serves the international, inter-sectoral and knowledge-transfer expectations of EI-02. Every activity is scaled to a single-fellow action, tied to a KPI (K1-K10 track the delivered artefacts; K11 tracks the reviewed Career Development Plan), and carries concrete actions both during the fellowship (inventory maintenance, MVP co-development, AgroVIR evaluation) and after it (the post-MSCA FMIS integration and exploitation roadmap and the Bulgarian replication route).
